Exhibit No. GNY-200 
 
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
 
 
 
LS POWER GRID NEW YORK CORPORATION I 
) 
Docket No. ER27-__-000 
NEW YORK INDEPENDENT SYSTEM 
 
) 
Docket No. EL26-69-000 
 OPERATOR, INC. 
 
) 
 
DIRECT TESTIMONY 
OF 
D. ERIC ARZOLA 
 
 
I. 
INTRODUCTION AND EXPERIENCE 
1 
Q. 
PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS. 
2 
A. 
My name is D. Eric Arzola.  My business address is 16150 Main Circle Drive, Suite 310, 
3 
Chesterfield, Missouri 63017. 
4 
Q. 
WITH WHAT ENTITY ARE YOU EMPLOYED? 
5 
A. 
I am employed as the Director of Transmission Rates at LS Power Development, LLC 
6 
(“LS Power Development”), the general partner and manager of LS Power Associates, 
7 
L.P. (“LS Power”), which is the indirect majority owner of LS Power Grid New York 
8 
Corporation I (“LSPGNY” or “Company”). 
9 
Q. 
ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU TESTIFYING IN THIS PROCEEDING? 
10 
A. 
I am testifying on behalf of LSPGNY. 
11 
Q. 
HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY FILED TESTIMONY BEFORE A REGULATORY 
12 
COMMISSION? 
13 
A. 
Yes.  I have submitted testimony in FERC Docket Nos. ER22-221, ER23-206, ER24-
14 
264, ER24-2668, ER25-321, ER25-2025, ER26-140, ER26-315, ER27-165, and ER27-
15 
482. 
16

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 2 of 20 
 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND 
1 
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE. 
2 
A. 
I have a Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics from Rice University in Houston, Texas, 
3 
and a Graduate Certificate in Energy Policy and Management from Portland State 
4 
University in Portland, Oregon.  I have over 22 years of experience in the energy 
5 
industry, with over 12 years focused on transmission cost of service rates, regulation, and 
6 
strategy.  I have been employed by LS Power Development since 2020, where I am 
7 
responsible for overseeing transmission rates for LS Power’s Federal Energy Regulatory 
8 
Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”) jurisdictional entities.  Prior to joining LS 
9 
Power, I held positions with similar responsibilities at GridLiance LLC and PacifiCorp. 
10 
II. 
PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY 
11 
Q. 
WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY? 
12 
A. 
The purpose of my testimony is to explain the revisions LSPGNY proposes to its 
13 
Formula Rate Template and Formula Rate Implementation Protocols so that LSPGNY 
14 
can recover the cost of transmission facilities built to serve large loads and covered by a 
15 
Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement (“CRA”) (“Covered Upgrades”), and credit the 
16 
amounts Eligible Customers pay under their CRAs toward its transmission revenue 
17 
requirement.  The revisions respond to the Commission’s June 18, 2026, order in Docket 
18 
No. EL26-69-000 (“Show Cause Order”).  Specifically, my testimony (i) describes the 
19 
large load cost recovery framework the revisions implement; (ii) describes the changes to 
20 
the Formula Rate Template, including new Attachments 1a and 2a; (iii) describes several 
21 
ministerial corrections to the existing Formula Rate Template; (iv) describes the changes 
22 
to the Formula Rate Implementation Protocols; (v) describes the exhibits I sponsor, 
23 
including illustrative examples; and (vi) explains why the revisions are just and 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 3 of 20 
 
reasonable.  The pro forma CRA, including how each Eligible Customer’s annual 
1 
Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution is established, is sponsored by LSPGNY 
2 
witness Mr. Hayes. 
3 
Q. 
PLEASE SUMMARIZE THE PROPOSED REVISIONS TO THE FORMULA 
4 
RATE TEMPLATE. 
5 
A. 
LSPGNY proposes the following changes: 
6 
• Add Attachment 2a – Project Plant Detail, to report plant and net investment 
7 
separately for the Marcy to New Scotland 345 kV Upgrade Project (“Segment A”) 
8 
and each Covered Upgrade; 
9 
• Use the project detail on Attachment 2a to calculate the revenue requirement of 
10 
each project on Attachment 4 – Incentives; 
11 
• Add Attachment 1a – Supplemental MTRC, to calculate, by Eligible Customer 
12 
and Covered Upgrade, the Supplemental MTRC and Annual Termination Fee 
13 
Remittances that make up Projected Large Load CRA Revenue, and to record the 
14 
Actual Large Load CRA Revenue LSPGNY receives; 
15 
• Credit Projected Large Load CRA Revenue in the Annual Projection, and Actual 
16 
Large Load CRA Revenue in the Annual Update, on a new Line 5a of Attachment 
17 
1 – Revenue Credits; 
18 
• Add lines to Appendix A that show the Large Load CRA Revenue the New York 
19 
Independent System Operator, Inc. (“NYISO”) will bill and remit to LSPGNY; 
20 
• Add a true-up of the Supplemental MTRC by Eligible Customer and Covered 
21 
Upgrade on Attachment 5 – True-Up; and 
22 
• Correct several ministerial errors in the existing Formula Rate Template. 
23

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 4 of 20 
 
LSPGNY also proposes limited changes to the Formula Rate Implementation Protocols to 
1 
define the new terms, add work paper and notice requirements, address how Large Load 
2 
CRA Revenue is reflected in the True-Up Adjustment, and address customer-specific 
3 
information. 
4 
Q. 
DO THE REVISIONS CHANGE HOW LSPGNY’S REVENUE REQUIREMENT 
5 
IS CALCULATED? 
6 
A. 
No.  The cost of service inputs, return, depreciation, taxes, and allocators are unchanged.  
7 
Covered Upgrades are included in LSPGNY’s rate base and revenue requirement in the 
8 
same manner as any other LSPGNY transmission plant.  The revisions add project-level 
9 
detail and a new revenue credit for Large Load CRA Revenue.  Absent any Covered 
10 
Upgrade or CRA, the revised Formula Rate Template produces the same revenue 
11 
requirement as the currently effective Formula Rate Template, apart from the ministerial 
12 
corrections described below. 
13 
Q. 
OTHER THAN YOUR TESTIMONY, ARE YOU SPONSORING ANY 
14 
EXHIBITS? 
15 
A. 
Yes.  I am sponsoring the following exhibits: 
16 
• Exhibit No. GNY-201, Clean Formula Rate Template; 
17 
• Exhibit No. GNY-202, Marked Formula Rate Template; 
18 
• Exhibit No. GNY-203, Clean Formula Rate Template in native Excel format with 
19 
all formulas intact; 
20 
• Exhibit No. GNY-204, Illustrative Formula Rate Template – Annual Projection; 
21 
• Exhibit No. GNY-205, Illustrative Formula Rate Template – Annual Update; 
22 
• Exhibit No. GNY-206, Clean Formula Rate Implementation Protocols; and 
23 
• Exhibit No. GNY-207, Marked Formula Rate Implementation Protocols. 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 5 of 20 
 
III. 
LSPGNY AND FORMULA RATE BACKGROUND 
1 
Q. 
PLEASE PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF LSPGNY AND ITS FORMULA RATE. 
2 
A. 
LSPGNY is a transmission-only company that owns Segment A, developed with the New 
3 
York Power Authority to meet the AC Transmission Public Policy Transmission Need.  
4 
LSPGNY’s formula rate consists of its Formula Rate Template (NYISO Open Access 
5 
Transmission Tariff (“OATT”) Section 6.10.7.2.1) and its Formula Rate Implementation 
6 
Protocols (Section 6.10.7.2.2) (together, the “Formula Rate”), which were accepted by 
7 
the Commission in Docket No. ER20-716.  LSPGNY’s revenue requirement is recovered 
8 
under Rate Schedule 10 of the NYISO OATT. 
9 
Q. 
HOW DOES THE FORMULA RATE OPERATE EACH YEAR? 
10 
A. 
By September 30, LSPGNY posts an Annual Projection of its revenue requirement for 
11 
the upcoming Rate Year.  By June 30 after each Rate Year, LSPGNY posts an Annual 
12 
Update using actual FERC Form No. 1 or other Company data.  The difference between 
13 
the revenue LSPGNY collected during the Rate Year and its actual revenue requirement, 
14 
with interest, is the True-up Adjustment, which is included in a later Annual Projection. 
15 
Q. 
WHY MUST LSPGNY REVISE ITS FORMULA RATE? 
16 
A. 
In the Show Cause Order, the Commission directed the NYISO and its transmission 
17 
owners to show cause why their tariffs remain just and reasonable or to propose changes 
18 
for integrating large loads.  Among other things, the Commission called for a mechanism 
19 
to ensure that large load payments are “credited toward transmission owners’ 
20 
transmission revenue requirements.”  LSPGNY’s current Formula Rate Template reports 
21 
plant values only in total and has no means of identifying the facilities built to serve large 
22 
loads or of crediting the amounts Eligible Customers pay under their CRAs.  The 
23 
revisions I describe provide that mechanism. 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 6 of 20 
 
IV. 
THE LARGE LOAD COST RECOVERY FRAMEWORK 
1 
Q. 
WHAT IS A CRA? 
2 
A. 
A CRA is an agreement between LSPGNY and an Eligible Customer taking transmission 
3 
service on behalf of a large load.  Under its CRA, the Eligible Customer commits to an 
4 
annual Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“Annual MTRC”) for each 
5 
Covered Upgrade built to serve the large load, for the term of the CRA.  The Annual 
6 
MTRC is calculated solely under the CRA.  The terms of the pro forma CRA, including 
7 
how the Annual MTRC is established, termination, and credit support requirements, are 
8 
described in the transmittal letter and the testimony of Mr. Hayes.  The Formula Rate 
9 
Template uses the Annual MTRC set by each CRA as an input. 
10 
Q. 
HOW ARE THE COSTS OF COVERED UPGRADES RECOVERED? 
11 
A. 
The cost of each Covered Upgrade is included in LSPGNY’s rate base and revenue 
12 
requirement and recovered under the NYISO OATT together with the cost of Segment A.  
13 
Each Eligible Customer pays transmission charges for the service it takes, like any other 
14 
transmission customer.  The transmission revenues that count toward an Eligible 
15 
Customer’s Annual MTRC, as determined under its CRA, are its “Qualifying 
16 
Transmission Revenues.” 
17 
Q. 
WHAT IS THE SUPPLEMENTAL MTRC? 
18 
A. 
The Supplemental MTRC is the amount, if any, by which an Eligible Customer’s Annual 
19 
MTRC for a Covered Upgrade exceeds its Qualifying Transmission Revenues for that 
20 
Covered Upgrade.  It requires the Eligible Customer to pay at least its committed Annual 
21 
MTRC each year, even if its load develops more slowly than expected.  The 
22 
Supplemental MTRC is measured separately for each Covered Upgrade and is never less 
23

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 7 of 20 
 
than zero, so Qualifying Transmission Revenues above the Annual MTRC on one 
1 
Covered Upgrade do not offset a shortfall on another. 
2 
Q. 
HOW IS THE SUPPLEMENTAL MTRC BILLED? 
3 
A. 
The Supplemental MTRC follows the same projection and true-up cycle as the rest of the 
4 
Formula Rate.  In each Annual Projection, LSPGNY projects each Eligible Customer’s 
5 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues and resulting Supplemental MTRC for the Rate Year.  
6 
The NYISO bills each active Eligible Customer its projected Supplemental MTRC in 
7 
equal monthly installments during the Rate Year and remits the amounts to LSPGNY.  In 
8 
the Annual Update, the Supplemental MTRC billed is compared to the Supplemental 
9 
MTRC based on actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues.  The difference is included, 
10 
without interest, in that Eligible Customer’s Supplemental MTRC in a later Annual 
11 
Projection. 
12 
Q. 
WHY IS THE SUPPLEMENTAL MTRC PROJECTED AND TRUED UP 
13 
RATHER THAN BILLED AFTER THE RATE YEAR? 
14 
A. 
Billing the projected amount during the Rate Year matches the timing of the 
15 
Supplemental MTRC credit to the Rate Year in which it reduces the revenue requirement, 
16 
spreads the Eligible Customer’s payments evenly over the year, and uses the projection 
17 
and true-up process that stakeholders already know.  Because each Eligible Customer’s 
18 
Supplemental MTRC is trued up to actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues, the 
19 
Eligible Customer is ultimately responsible for its full Annual MTRC.  Any difference 
20 
between the projected and actual amounts is corrected in a later Rate Year. 
21 
Q. 
WHAT HAPPENS IF AN ELIGIBLE CUSTOMER TERMINATES ITS CRA? 
22 
A. 
If an Eligible Customer terminates its CRA after an applicable in-service date, it pays a 
23 
Termination Fee equal to its Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility less any 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 8 of 20 
 
Supplemental MTRC already billed and remaining unpaid as of the effective termination 
1 
date, as provided in CRA Section 3.3.4. The NYISO collects and holds that fee. The 
2 
excluded unpaid bills remain separately payable as Large Load Charges, and receipt of 
3 
the Termination Fee in full discharges only the remaining responsibility included in the 
4 
fee, not those unpaid bills.  The NYISO remits to LSPGNY the scheduled Annual 
5 
Termination Fee Remittances determined under CRA Section 3.3.6 and the Termination 
6 
Fee Remittance Worksheet in Schedule 5. Those scheduled amounts reflect applicable 
7 
partial-year proration, are limited to the available Termination Fee Balance, and include 
8 
any residual balance and actual account earnings required to be remitted with the final 
9 
installment.  LSPGNY credits the Annual Termination Fee Remittances in the same way 
10 
as the Supplemental MTRC, with projected remittances credited in the Annual Projection 
11 
and actual remittances received credited in the Annual Update.  The Covered Upgrade 
12 
remains in rate base.  The terms governing termination are described in the testimony of 
13 
Mr. Hayes. 
14 
Q. 
HOW DOES THE FORMULA RATE TREAT LARGE LOAD CRA REVENUE? 
15 
A. 
The Supplemental MTRC and Annual Termination Fee Remittances (together, “Large 
16 
Load CRA Revenue”) are credited against LSPGNY’s revenue requirement as a revenue 
17 
credit.  The credit reduces the revenue requirement dollar for dollar, so the benefit goes to 
18 
customers rather than to LSPGNY.  In the Annual Projection, LSPGNY credits the Large 
19 
Load CRA Revenue it projects for the Rate Year (“Projected Large Load CRA 
20 
Revenue”).  In the Annual Update, it credits the Large Load CRA Revenue it receives 
21 
during the Rate Year (“Actual Large Load CRA Revenue”): Supplemental MTRC 
22 
payments the NYISO collects and remits, Applied Security Proceeds applied to 
23 
Supplemental MTRC obligations and remitted by the NYISO, amounts LSPGNY 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 9 of 20 
 
recovers directly from an Eligible Customer and applies to Supplemental MTRC 
1 
obligations, and Annual Termination Fee Remittances. 
2 
Q. 
DO THE COVERED UPGRADES RECEIVE THE INCENTIVES GRANTED 
3 
FOR SEGMENT A? 
4 
A. 
No.  The return on equity (“ROE”) incentive the Commission granted for Segment A in 
5 
Docket No. ER20-716 applies only to Segment A, as entered on Attachment 4, 
6 
Column (e) and documented under Note D.  Covered Upgrades are separately identified 
7 
in LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate and use the capital structure and generally applicable 
8 
return components applicable to LS Power Grid under Rate Schedule 10, including any 
9 
Commission-approved generally applicable return on equity incentive, as applicable. 
10 
Covered Upgrades do not receive return on equity incentives that are specific to the AC 
11 
Transmission Project or become subject to the AC Transmission Project’s Competitive 
12 
Bid Concession, cost cap, or other project-specific cost-containment commitments. 
13 
V. 
LSPGNY’S PROPOSED FORMULA RATE TEMPLATE CHANGES 
14 
Q. 
WHY IS ATTACHMENT 2A NEEDED? 
15 
A. 
The existing Formula Rate Template reports transmission plant only in total.  To identify 
16 
the investment in each Covered Upgrade, the Formula Rate Template must report 
17 
Segment A and each Covered Upgrade separately.  Attachment 2a provides that detail. 
18 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE ATTACHMENT 2A. 
19 
A. 
Attachment 2a has five sections, each with a line for Segment A and lines for Covered 
20 
Upgrades.  Additional project lines may be added as Covered Upgrades are placed in 
21 
service. 
22 
• Section 1 reports monthly transmission gross plant in service and its 13-month 
23 
average.  The monthly totals populate Attachment 2, Lines 2–14. 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 10 of 20 
 
• Section 2 reports monthly transmission accumulated depreciation and its 13-
1 
month average.  The monthly totals populate Attachment 2, Lines 78–90. 
2 
• Sections 3 and 4 report unamortized regulatory assets and unamortized abandoned 
3 
plant by project. 
4 
• Section 5 calculates each project’s net investment (Line 1 – Line 2 + Line 3 + 
5 
Line 4), which is used on Attachment 4, Column (b).  The total ties to Appendix 
6 
A, Line 103. 
7 
Because the Attachment 2a totals flow to Attachment 2, total plant and accumulated 
8 
depreciation are unchanged.  Project names entered on Attachment 2a carry to 
9 
Attachment 4, Column (a), and Attachment 5, Lines 2–2d. 
10 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE THE REVISIONS TO ATTACHMENT 1. 
11 
A. 
LSPGNY proposes a new Line 5a, Large Load CRA Revenue – Supplemental MTRC 
12 
and Annual Termination Fee Remittances, which will be included in Total Revenue 
13 
Credits on Line 6.  New Note 4 describes the new line.  In an Annual Projection, Line 5a 
14 
equals the Projected Large Load CRA Revenue, the Attachment 1a total.  In an Annual 
15 
Update, Line 5a equals the Actual Large Load CRA Revenue received during the Rate 
16 
Year, from new Lines 24–34 of Attachment 1a.  Line 2 of the account detail on 
17 
Attachment 1 shows the Large Load CRA Revenue recorded in Account 456, and any 
18 
difference from Line 5a is reconciled in the work papers required by the Formula Rate 
19 
Implementation Protocols.  Qualifying Transmission Revenues are not credited on Line 
20 
5a because they are already part of the transmission revenue LSPGNY collects. 
21 
Q. 
WHY IS LARGE LOAD CRA REVENUE TREATED AS A REVENUE CREDIT? 
22 
A. 
Revenue credits are the Formula Rate Template’s existing means of passing revenue back 
23 
to customers.  Crediting Large Load CRA Revenue on Attachment 1 reduces LSPGNY’s 
24

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 11 of 20 
 
revenue requirement on Appendix A, Line 2 and, through Line 106, the base carrying 
1 
charge used to calculate each project’s revenue requirement on Attachment 4.  No new 
2 
allocation method is needed. 
3 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE THE NEW ATTACHMENT 1A. 
4 
A. 
Attachment 1a calculates Projected Large Load CRA Revenue, and records Actual Large 
5 
Load CRA Revenue, by Eligible Customer and Covered Upgrade for the Rate Year.  
6 
Each of Lines 1–10 is one Eligible Customer and Covered Upgrade: 
7 
• Columns 1–3 identify the Eligible Customer, the Covered Upgrade, and its status 
8 
(Active or Terminated); 
9 
• Column 4 is the projected Qualifying Transmission Revenues, from the 
10 
workpaper on Lines 14–23, which calculates them as forecast load (MW) 
11 
multiplied by billing hours and the applicable transmission rate; 
12 
• Column 5 is the Annual MTRC under the Eligible Customer’s CRA; 
13 
• Column 6 is, for an active Eligible Customer, the Supplemental MTRC (Column 
14 
5 less Column 4, but not less than zero) and, for a terminated Eligible Customer, 
15 
the scheduled Annual Termination Fee Remittance for the Rate Year, entered 
16 
separately in Column K from the Termination Fee Remittance Worksheet in 
17 
Schedule 5 of the applicable CRA; 
18 
• Column 7 is any prior-period true-up adjustment from Attachment 5; and 
19 
• Column 8 is the total (Column 6 plus Column 7). 
20 
Line 11 totals each column, and Lines 12 and 13 separate the totals for active and 
21 
terminated Eligible Customers.  In an Annual Projection, the Line 11 total is credited on 
22 
Attachment 1, Line 5a.  In an Annual Update, Attachment 1a uses actual Qualifying 
23

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 12 of 20 
 
Transmission Revenues to determine the actual Supplemental MTRC for the true-up on 
1 
Attachment 5, and its labels change from “Projected” to “Actual.” 
2 
Q. 
WHAT DO NEW LINES 24–34 OF ATTACHMENT 1A SHOW? 
3 
A. 
Lines 24–34 are completed in the Annual Update.  For each Eligible Customer and 
4 
Covered Upgrade, they show the opening unpaid Supplemental MTRC, the Supplemental 
5 
MTRC billed during the Rate Year, and the amounts LSPGNY received during the Rate 
6 
Year: Supplemental MTRC payments the NYISO collected and remitted (Column (c)), 
7 
Applied Security Proceeds applied to Supplemental MTRC obligations and remitted by 
8 
the NYISO (Column (d)), amounts LSPGNY recovered directly from the Eligible 
9 
Customer and applied to Supplemental MTRC obligations (Column (e)), and Annual 
10 
Termination Fee Remittances (Column (f)).  Column (g), the sum of Columns (c) through 
11 
(f), is the Actual Large Load CRA Revenue, and its total on Line 34 is credited on 
12 
Attachment 1, Line 5a.  Column (h) is the closing unpaid Supplemental MTRC, which 
13 
carries forward to the next Annual Update so that a later collection is identified and 
14 
credited once, in the Rate Year in which it is received. 
15 
Q. 
WHAT IS SHOWN IN THE NEW LINES ON APPENDIX A? 
16 
A. 
New lines a1 through c on Appendix A show the Large Load CRA Revenue the NYISO 
17 
will bill and remit during the Rate Year: the projected Supplemental MTRC (line a1), 
18 
prior-period true-up adjustments (line a2), the total Supplemental MTRC to be billed 
19 
(line a), Annual Termination Fee Remittances (line b), and total Large Load CRA 
20 
Revenue (line c), which is included in Line 2.  New Note R describes these lines.  These 
21 
informational lines are populated for the Annual Projection.  They do not change the 
22 
calculation of the Net Adjusted Revenue Requirement on Line 5. 
23

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 13 of 20 
 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE THE REVISIONS TO ATTACHMENT 5. 
1 
A. 
LSPGNY proposes a new section, Lines 14–24, that trues up the Supplemental MTRC 
2 
for each active Eligible Customer and Covered Upgrade.  It compares the Supplemental 
3 
MTRC billed during the Rate Year to the Supplemental MTRC based on actual 
4 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues.  The difference, without interest, flows to 
5 
Attachment 1a, Column 7, for that Eligible Customer and Covered Upgrade.  In addition, 
6 
project names on Lines 2–2d now come from Attachment 2a, the interest calculation on 
7 
Lines 2a–2d now uses the same formula as Line 2 (previously it was zero), the notes are 
8 
moved below the calculations, Note 2 clarifies that revenue received excludes Large 
9 
Load CRA Revenue, and new Note 5 describes the Supplemental MTRC true-up. 
10 
Q. 
WHY IS THE SUPPLEMENTAL MTRC TRUED UP BY ELIGIBLE 
11 
CUSTOMER? 
12 
A. 
The difference between projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues relates to 
13 
a specific Eligible Customer’s commitment.  Truing it up in that Eligible Customer’s 
14 
Supplemental MTRC keeps responsibility for the Annual MTRC with that Eligible 
15 
Customer, rather than with other customers.  True-up adjustments for terminated Eligible 
16 
Customers are addressed under the CRA. 
17 
Q. 
HOW DOES THIS TRUE-UP DIFFER FROM THE TRUE-UP OF LARGE LOAD 
18 
CRA REVENUE IN THE FORMULA RATE? 
19 
A. 
They address different things.  The true-up by Eligible Customer on Attachment 5 
20 
corrects the forecast of Qualifying Transmission Revenues.  It compares the 
21 
Supplemental MTRC billed with the Supplemental MTRC based on actual Qualifying 
22 
Transmission Revenues, and the difference, without interest, adjusts that Eligible 
23 
Customer’s Supplemental MTRC in a later Annual Projection.  It does not depend on 
24 
whether the billed amount was paid.  Separately, the Formula Rate’s existing True-Up 
25

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 14 of 20 
 
Adjustment compares the Projected Large Load CRA Revenue credited in the Annual 
1 
Projection with the Actual Large Load CRA Revenue received.  If a billed amount is not 
2 
received during the Rate Year, LSPGNY’s actual revenue requirement is higher than 
3 
projected, and the difference is included, with interest, in the True-Up Adjustment in a 
4 
later Annual Projection, in the same manner as any other difference between projected 
5 
and actual revenue requirement.  The Eligible Customer remains liable for the unpaid 
6 
amount, which is subject to the CRA’s security and collection provisions, and any later 
7 
receipt is credited in the Rate Year in which it is received.  Exhibit No. GNY-205 
8 
illustrates both true-ups. 
9 
Q. 
HOW IS CUSTOMER-SPECIFIC INFORMATION ADDRESSED? 
10 
A. 
Attachment 1a reports information by Eligible Customer and Covered Upgrade.  Under 
11 
new Section 8 of the Formula Rate Implementation Protocols, which I describe below, 
12 
customer-specific information is treated as confidential, LSPGNY posts and files 
13 
versions of its Annual Projection and Annual Update that aggregate or redact that 
14 
information, and the unredacted information is available under the Formula Rate 
15 
Implementation Protocols’ existing confidentiality procedures. 
16 
Q. 
ARE THERE OTHER CHANGES TO THE FORMULA RATE TEMPLATE? 
17 
A. 
Yes.  Attachments 1a and 2a are added to the Index.  In addition, LSPGNY proposes the 
18 
ministerial corrections described in the next section. 
19 
VI. 
MINISTERIAL CORRECTIONS 
20 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE THE MINISTERIAL CORRECTIONS LSPGNY 
21 
PROPOSES. 
22 
A. 
LSPGNY proposes the following corrections to the existing Formula Rate Template: 
23

Exhibit No. GNY-200 
Page 15 of 20 
 
• Attachment 4, Column (d): the heading now references Appendix A, Line 98, the 
1 
line its formula uses, rather than Line 94;  
2 
• Attachment 4, Column (n):  the heading now reads (Col. (l) x Col. (m)) rather 
3 
than (Col. (l) x Col. (n)); and 
4 
• Attachment 5, Notes 3 and 4: typographical errors are corrected. 
5 
Q. 
DO THESE CORRECTIONS CHANGE THE FORMULA RATE 
6 
METHODOLOGY? 
7 
A. 
No.  Each correction conforms a formula or label to the methodology the Commission 
8 
accepted in Docket No. ER20-716. 
9 
VII. 
FORMULA RATE IMPLEMENTATION PROTOCOLS 
10 
Q. 
WHAT CHANGES DOES LSPGNY PROPOSE TO THE FORMULA RATE 
11 
IMPLEMENTATION PROTOCOLS? 
12 
A. 
LSPGNY proposes the following changes: 
13 
• A new paragraph following the introductory paragraph defines “Cost Recovery 
14 
Agreement” (“CRA”), “Eligible Customer,” “Annual MTRC,” “Qualifying 
15 
Transmission Revenues,” “Supplemental MTRC,” “Large Load CRA Revenue,” 
16 
“Projected Large Load CRA Revenue,” and “Actual Large Load CRA Revenue” 
17 
as used in the Formula Rate Implementation Protocols and the Formula Rate 
18 
Template.  These definitions are tied to the CRA, and other capitalized terms used 
19 
in connection with a CRA have the meanings given in the CRA; 
20
